meta_description: Nintendo Switch parental controls on the console itself: daily play-time limits, PIN, restrictions, play activity and network clock. No phone app, no Nintendo account, no internet.
hero_title: Nintendo Switch parental controls, right on the console
hero_sub: No phone app, no Nintendo account, no internet.
hero_text: PlayGuard brings the settings of Nintendo's Parental Controls phone app onto a modded console. It drives the console's own controls — the limit, the PIN, the warnings, the suspension — so nothing runs in the background.
cfw_text: PlayGuard uses the console's restricted parental-control service, some of it through debug commands. Use at your own risk.
features_title: Everything the phone app does, on the console
f_timer_text: The same every day or one per day, profiles, extra time or no more play today in one press.
f_activity_text: Time per game and per account, charts, export to CSV, JSON, XLSX or PDF.
f_restrictions_text: Restriction level, age rating, PIN, temporary unlock, “{{app:console_lock/title}}” in one switch.
f_console_text: The network clock set from public time servers, so the timer counts right on a console that never reaches Nintendo, and a check of the installed games.
f_app_text: Unlink it, even on a second-hand console.
f_history_text: Every change is logged and can be undone.
f_notices_text: A bell gathers what needs you — an alarm off, a clock drifting, changes made elsewhere — with the fix one press away.
f_languages_text: The 15 languages of the console, light and dark themes.
simulator_title: Try it before you install it
simulator_text: The real PlayGuard runs in your browser against a simulated console: browse every screen, try a locked or unlocked console, a limit reached, another firmware.
install_1: Search for PlayGuard in the Homebrew App Store or sphaira, and install it.
install_2: Extract playguard.zip from the latest release to the root of the SD card.
install_3: Launch it over a game, with a parent's user.
store_pending: Not available yet: PlayGuard's listing is still awaiting approval. Install it by hand for now.
start_1: Open PlayGuard: the “{{app:onboarding/title}}” guide sets the PIN and the daily limit.
start_2: Still linked to the phone app? “{{app:tabs/security}} › {{app:pairing/unlink}}”, or its next sync overwrites what you set.
start_3: Network clock inaccurate? “{{app:tabs/console}} › {{app:tabs/clock}} › {{app:clock/measure}}”, then set it.
compat_text: PlayGuard runs on a Nintendo Switch with Atmosphère, launched from hbmenu, sphaira or the Homebrew App Store. A firmware newer than the ones it knows opens read-only until a release supports it. There is no Switch 2 version: there is no Atmosphère for it.
faq_closed_q: Does it keep working once PlayGuard is closed?
faq_closed_a: Yes. The limit, the PIN, the warnings and the suspension are the console's own parental controls: PlayGuard only changes their settings, and nothing of it runs in the background.
faq_offline_q: Does it need the internet, a Nintendo account or the phone app?
faq_offline_a: No. Everything is set on the console. The play timer only needs the network clock to have been set once: from public time servers, or from the console clock on a console without internet.
faq_ban_q: Can it get the console banned?
faq_ban_a: PlayGuard never contacts Nintendo: online, it only reaches public time servers and GitHub. What gets consoles banned is custom firmware going online to Nintendo. No ban tied to parental-control or clock changes is documented; that is not a guarantee.
faq_children_q: Can each child have their own limit?
faq_children_a: No: the console's play timer has one limit for the whole console. A replacement sysmodule can set one per user account, but it replaces the console's parental controls with its own.
faq_sysmodule_a: PlayGuard sets the console's own parental controls, the ones Nintendo maintains, and runs only while you use it. A replacement sysmodule runs in the background all the time and takes their place: it can do more (a limit per child), but it is one more program that a firmware or Atmosphère update can break. Pick one, not both.
faq_emummc_a: Each has its own parental controls, and PlayGuard only sees those of the system it runs on: set them on both, or hide hekate's boot menu so that a child cannot pick the other one.
faq_switch2_q: Does it work on a Switch 2?
faq_switch2_a: No: there is no Atmosphère for the Switch 2.
faq_free_a: Yes: free and open-source software, under the GNU GPL v3.
